name: Lip underpainting

card.summary: A makeup technique that contours or shades the lips beneath lipstick so they look fuller and more defined.

quick.overview:
Lip underpainting applies a shade of liner or color under or around the lip color to shape the lips. It belongs to the family of lip liner techniques, which smooth uneven edges and create more definition between lips and skin.

The visual aim is a fuller, more sculpted mouth. Lip liners also keep lipstick from feathering.
quick.how: Liner, often matched to lip color, is used to outline or fill the lips before lipstick. Harder pencils give sharper lines; in the 1990s, dark brown liner under lighter lipstick was common.
quick.risks: Makeup ingredients can irritate skin or cause allergy in some people.

lead: Lip liners are cosmetic pencils used to shape the lips, prevent lipstick from feathering, make the lips appear fuller, and sharpen the line between lip and skin.[1] Underpainting extends this idea by shading under the final lip color, a technique popularized on social media.

Liners resemble lipsticks but contain more wax and pigment and less oil for precision; they have been used since the 1920s, with Clara Bow, Marlene Dietrich and Marilyn Monroe cited as early adopters.[1]

chain: Shade or liner placed under lipstick
angle.text: It uses shading and outline to change how full and defined the lips appear.

paras: Outlining traces the lip edge to define shape and hold color; filling colors the whole lip; clear liner smooths lips without changing color.[1] Shades are usually matched to lipstick for a natural look.[1]
